question_text: A 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus comes to the physician because of a 4-day history of fever, chills, nausea, and abdominal pain. He does not use illicit drugs. His temperature is 39°C (102.2°F). Physical examination shows right upper quadrant tenderness. Ultrasonography of the abdomen shows a 6-cm solitary, fluid-filled cavity in the right hepatic lobe. CT-guided percutaneous aspiration of the cavity produces yellowish-green fluid. Culture of the aspirated fluid grows gram-negative, lactose-fermenting rods. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the color of the aspirated fluid?
